# Ricky Dicky's Schedule Time: API for agents

> A group scheduling app at https://rickrothbart.com/scheduling/. Someone creates
> an event with candidate dates and hours, shares the link, and each person marks
> when they are free. Everything the website does goes through the JSON API below,
> so an agent can do all of it: create events, read who is free, and add
> availability.

## Base URL

Fetch `https://rickrothbart.com/scheduling/config.json`; the API base is its
`apiUrl` field. At the time of writing it is:

    https://6v2bktmvcmgbmsy3bikb74v5eq0goxlb.lambda-url.us-west-1.on.aws/

Paths below are relative to that base. Requests and responses are JSON. No API key.

## Times: read this first

Every time is a UTC string. The event's `timezone` is only for display; convert
to and from it yourself.

- Specific-date events: `HHmm-DDMMYYYY`, e.g. `1700-25102026` = 17:00 UTC on 25 Oct 2026.
- Days-of-the-week events: `HHmm-d`, where `d` is 0=Sunday … 6=Saturday, e.g. `1700-3`.
  Tell the two apart by length (13 vs 6 characters).
- An event's `times` lists the **hour** slots on offer (minutes always `00`).
- A person's `availability` uses **15-minute** slots: each offered hour `HH00`
  splits into `HH00`, `HH15`, `HH30`, `HH45` (same date part).
  Only send slots that fall inside the event's offered hours; the API doesn't check.

Example: an event in America/Los_Angeles offering 10:00–12:00 local on 25 Oct 2026
(UTC−7) has `times` `["1700-25102026", "1800-25102026"]`, and someone free
10:00–11:00 local sends `["1700-25102026", "1715-25102026", "1730-25102026", "1745-25102026"]`.

## Endpoints

### POST /event: create an event
Body: `{"name": "Team lunch", "times": ["1700-25102026", ...], "timezone": "America/Los_Angeles"}`
(`name` optional; a random one like "Puzzled Hangout" is generated.)
201 → `{"id": "team-lunch-123456", "name", "times", "timezone", "created_at", "edit_key"}`
(`created_at` is Unix seconds.)
`edit_key` is returned only here and is needed to edit the event later. Keep it
private and give it only to the person who asked you to create the event.
Share link for people: `https://rickrothbart.com/scheduling/event/?id=<id>`
The creator's private edit link is `https://rickrothbart.com/scheduling/event/?id=<id>&key=<edit_key>`;
opening it in a browser lets them edit the event on the website too.

### PATCH /event/{id}: edit an event (creator only)
Header: `X-Edit-Key: <edit_key>`. Body: any of `{"name", "times", "timezone"}`;
omitted fields are kept, and `times` replaces the whole list.
The id and share link stay the same, and people's availability is kept (slots
that are no longer offered just stop showing).
200 → event. 403 → missing or wrong edit key. 404 → unknown event.
If you only have the edit link, the key is its `key` query parameter.

### GET /event/{id}: event details
200 → same shape as above. 404 if unknown.

### GET /event/{id}/people: everyone's availability
200 → `[{"name": "Alice", "availability": ["1700-25102026", ...], "created_at"}]`
People who haven't marked any times yet are left out.

### GET /event/{id}/people/{name}: sign in or sign up
Names are per event and case-insensitive. The first call with a new name creates
that person (with empty availability); later calls sign in.
Optional password: header `Authorization: Bearer <base64 of the password>`.
If the person was created with a password, every later call for them needs it.
200 → person. 401 → wrong password.

### PATCH /event/{id}/people/{name}: set availability
Body: `{"availability": ["1700-25102026", ...]}`. This **replaces** the whole list.
Same `Authorization` header as above if the person has a password.
The person must exist first (call the GET above). 200 → person; 401; 404.

URL-encode `{id}` and `{name}` (e.g. spaces as `%20`).

## Recipes

Find the best time: GET the event and `/people`, count how many people list each
15-minute slot, and report the slots with the highest count, converted to the
event's timezone, with who is free and who isn't.

Add someone's availability: GET `/event/{id}/people/{name}` (creates them), then
PATCH their full list of free 15-minute slots.

Create an event for a group: POST `/event` with the hour slots converted to UTC,
then share the link above, and give the creator their private edit link.

Change an event's dates or hours: GET the event, build the new full `times`
list, and PATCH it with the edit key.

## Example

    API=$(curl -s https://rickrothbart.com/scheduling/config.json | jq -r .apiUrl)
    curl -s -X POST "${API}event" -H 'content-type: application/json' \
      -d '{"name":"Team lunch","times":["1700-25102026","1800-25102026"],"timezone":"America/Los_Angeles"}'
    curl -s "${API}event/team-lunch-123456/people/Alice"
    curl -s -X PATCH "${API}event/team-lunch-123456/people/Alice" -H 'content-type: application/json' \
      -d '{"availability":["1700-25102026","1715-25102026","1730-25102026","1745-25102026"]}'
    curl -s "${API}event/team-lunch-123456/people"

## Etiquette

This is a small personal app for friends. Don't change someone's availability
unless they asked you to, and don't create events in bulk.
